items.q: In quot cohortēs singulae legiōnēs dīviduntur?
items.en: Into how many cohorts is each legion divided?
items.hint: a distributive numeral ('ten each') in the accusative after in

items.q: Quibus armīs legiōnāriī armātī sunt?
items.en: With what weapons are the legionaries armed?
items.hint: ablatives of means with the participle armātī

items.q: Quid est signum legiōnis?
items.en: What is the standard of a legion?
items.hint: the nominative predicate, with a relative clause in the passive (fertur)

items.q: Quandō cohortēs ad pugnam īnstruuntur?
items.en: When are the cohorts drawn up for battle?
items.hint: cum + perfect indicative (a general condition); ad pugnandum is ad + gerund

items.q: Quid dux ante proelium mīlitēs suōs hortātur?
items.en: What does the general urge his soldiers to do before battle?
items.hint: hortātur (deponent) ut + present subjunctive

items.q: Quōmodo castra Rōmāna mūniuntur?
items.en: How is a Roman camp fortified?
items.hint: ablatives of means; locō ad dēfendendum idōneō uses ad + gerund

items.q: Cūr Aemilius puer gladiōs ligneōs sibi faciēbat?
items.en: Why did Aemilius as a boy make himself wooden swords?
items.hint: a purpose clause: ut + imperfect subjunctive; septem annōs nātus gives his age

items.q: Cūr patrī voluntās fīliī nōn placēbat?
items.en: Why did his son's wish displease the father?
items.hint: a causal cum clause with the imperfect subjunctive; studēre takes the dative (litterīs)

items.q: Quō pater Aemilium ad exercitum mīsit?
items.en: Where did the father send Aemilius to join the army?
items.hint: in + accusative for place to which; the ut clause at the end gives the purpose

items.q: Ā quibus virtūs Aemiliī laudātur?
items.en: By whom is Aemilius' courage praised?
items.hint: the ablative of agent after ab with a passive verb

items.q: Quālem esse Aemilium ex litterīs prīvātīs appāret?
items.en: What state is Aemilius in, as appears from his private letters?
items.hint: an indirect statement with a perfect passive infinitive (fatīgātum esse); vītā mīlitārī is an ablative of means

items.q: Quandō Aemilia litterās novissimās ā frātre accēpit?
items.en: When did Aemilia receive the latest letter from her brother?
items.hint: a Roman date: prīdiē + accusative ('the day before the Kalends of June')

items.q: Ante quot diēs epistula Aemiliae scrīpta erat?
items.en: How many days earlier had Aemilia's letter been written?
items.hint: ante + accusative; the letter is dated by the Kalends of May

items.q: Quot diēbus celer tabellārius iter trāns Alpēs cōnficere potest?
items.en: In how many days can a fast courier complete the journey across the Alps?
items.hint: an ablative of time within which (quīndecim diēbus)

items.q: Fruunturne Aemilia et Iūlius bonā valētūdine?
items.en: Are Aemilia and Julius in good health?
items.hint: a yes/no question with -ne; fruor takes the ablative, inside an indirect statement after cognōvī

items.q: Quid Aemilius optat?
items.en: What does Aemilius wish?
answers: utinam Rōmae esset aut soror apud eum esset
Rōmae esse aut sorōrem apud sē esse
ut Rōmae esset aut soror apud sē esset
items.hint: utinam + imperfect subjunctive: a wish that cannot come true now

items.q: Cūr Aemilius haec frūstrā optat?
items.en: Why does Aemilius wish these things in vain?
items.hint: a causal cum clause with the present subjunctive (possit); trānsferrī is a passive infinitive

items.q: Quid Aemilius faceret, sī Mercurius esset?
items.en: What would Aemilius do if he were Mercury?
items.hint: a present contrary-to-fact condition: sī + imperfect subjunctive … imperfect subjunctive; ventō is an ablative of comparison

items.q: Quid hostēs facerent, nisi legiōnēs fīnēs imperiī dēfenderent?
items.en: What would the enemy do if the legions were not defending the frontiers?
items.hint: a contrary-to-fact condition: nisi + imperfect subjunctive … imperfect subjunctive (trānsīrent, pervenīrent)

items.q: Cūr Aemiliō nūllum ōtium fuit ad epistulam scrībendam?
items.en: Why did Aemilius have no leisure for writing a letter?
items.hint: a causal cum clause with the perfect subjunctive (habuerim); ad epistulam scrībendam is ad + gerundive

items.q: Quandō in castra nūntiātum est hostēs flūmen trānsīsse?
items.en: When was it reported in camp that the enemy had crossed the river?
items.hint: an ablative of time when (mediā nocte); the report is an indirect statement with a perfect infinitive

items.q: Quid mīlitēs prīmō mīrābantur?
items.en: What did the soldiers wonder at first?
items.hint: an indirect question with the pluperfect subjunctive; cum … cēpissent is a cum clause with the pluperfect subjunctive

items.q: Quid Aemilius dubitāre coeperat?
items.en: What had Aemilius begun to doubt?
items.hint: an indirect question with num and the pluperfect subjunctive (dīxisset)

items.q: Cūr nostrī prīmum impetum facile sustinuērunt?
items.en: Why did our men easily withstand the first attack?
items.hint: a causal cum clause with the imperfect subjunctive; ad castra dēfendenda is ad + gerundive (purpose)

items.q: Quā portā equitātus noster ērūpit?
items.en: Through which gate did our cavalry burst out?
items.hint: an ablative of the way by which; cum … pugnātum esset is an impersonal passive in a cum clause

items.q: Cūr aliī hostēs in flūmen sē iēcērunt?
items.en: Why did some of the enemy throw themselves into the river?
items.hint: a purpose clause with the imperfect subjunctive; natandō is a gerund in the ablative; ad eōs persequendōs is ad + gerundive

items.q: Quot mīlia hominum hostēs eō proeliō āmīsērunt?
items.en: How many thousand men did the enemy lose in that battle?
items.hint: a numeral with mīlia (neuter plural); hominum is a partitive genitive

items.q: Ubi Aemilius sagittā vulnerātus est?
items.en: Where was Aemilius wounded by an arrow?
items.hint: in + ablative (in bracchiō laevō); sagittā is an ablative of means

items.q: Cūr dux virtūtem mīlitum laudāvit?
items.en: Why did the general praise the soldiers' courage?
items.hint: quod + pluperfect subjunctive: a reason reported as the general's own; cum … salūtātus esset is a cum clause

items.q: Cūr lēgātī Germānōrum ad castra vēnērunt?
items.en: Why did the Germans' envoys come to the camp?
items.hint: a purpose clause: ut + imperfect subjunctive of a deponent verb

items.q: Quōmodo Pūblius Valerius cecidit?
items.en: How did Publius Valerius fall?
items.hint: an ablative of means with a perfect participle; cum … vellet is a cum clause with the imperfect subjunctive

items.q: Quid Aemilius nunc optat dē patre suō?
items.en: What does Aemilius now wish about his father?
items.hint: utinam + pluperfect subjunctive: a wish about the past that did not come true

items.q: Quem poētam Aemilius praecipuē ōderat?
items.en: Which poet did Aemilius particularly hate?
items.hint: the accusative object of ōderam (a pluperfect with imperfect meaning)

items.q: Quid Aemilius fēcisset, sī iam tum Tibullum vērum dīxisse intellēxisset?
items.en: What would Aemilius have done if he had understood back then that Tibullus was right?
items.hint: a past contrary-to-fact condition: sī + pluperfect subjunctive … pluperfect subjunctive

items.q: Quid Aemilia aliōs monēre dēbet?
items.en: What should Aemilia urge others to do?
items.hint: monētō is a future imperative; the command continues with ut + present subjunctive
